Building and Running

examples/general/logfile.cpp, one source file built by examples/CMakeLists.txt as logfile (cmake-build/examples/logfile on Linux, cmake-build\examples\Release\logfile.exe on Windows) and run by tests/run_tests.sh. See Building and Running for the build commands. The comment at the top of the file describes the program. Back to the example programs.

Log file demo. Several threads write time-stamped lines to one
LogFile at the same time; each line is written whole.

Usage: logfile [file_name]
*/
// ----------------------------------------------------------- // 
#include "gxdlcode.h"

#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>
#include "logfile.h"

using namespace datareel;

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
  std::string fname = argc > 1 ? argv[1] : "testlog.log";
  LogFile log;
  if(!log.OverWrite(fname)) {
    std::cerr << "Cannot create " << fname << "\n";
    return 1;
  }
  log.WriteLine("Log started");

  std::vector<std::thread> threads;
  for(int t = 1; t <= 4; t++) {
    threads.emplace_back([&log, t] {
      for(int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) {
        log.WriteLine("thread " + std::to_string(t) + " message " + 
                      std::to_string(i));
      }
    });
  }
  for(auto &th : threads) th.join();

  log << "A line built with operator<<: " << 42 << "\n";
  log.WriteLine("Log finished");
  log.Close();
  std::cout << "Wrote 23 lines to " << fname << "\n";
  return 0;
}
